jobs.name: Security & RBAC Posture Audit
jobs.prompt: Run the daily fleet security and RBAC posture audit. Read the SOP at 'governance/compliance_audit_sop.md' in your profile home — all 496 lines of it, before you run anything. Its sixteen checks are section 2, lines 115-395, so a read that stops early skips almost the entire audit and reports a clean fleet it never looked at. Section 2 opens by running the collector (`skills/fleet-audit/scripts/collect.py compliance-audit`) with --workspace set to the workspace start returned, redirecting its stdout to /opt/data/scratch/manifest_compliance-audit.json: run it before evaluating any check by hand, read the manifest the way section 2 says, and pass the same file to finish as --manifest-file. Then execute it exactly, using the fleet-audit skill to open and close the audit run.

jobs.name: AI Workload Security Audit
jobs.prompt: Run the daily AI workload security audit. Read the SOP at 'governance/ai_security_audit_sop.md' in your profile home — all 300 lines of it, before you run anything. Its six checks are section 3, lines 133-222, so a read that stops early skips almost the entire audit and reports a clean fleet it never looked at. Section 3 opens by running the collector (`skills/fleet-audit/scripts/collect.py ai-security-audit`) with --workspace set to the workspace start returned, redirecting its stdout to /opt/data/scratch/manifest_ai-security-audit.json: run it before evaluating any check by hand, read the manifest the way section 3 says, and pass the same file to finish as --manifest-file. Section 2 defines which workloads count as AI workloads; on a cluster running none the six checks still ran and matched nothing, so record all six in checks_run with the collector's command — never leave checks_run empty, which the validator rejects. Then execute it exactly, using the fleet-audit skill to open and close the audit run.
